title: Animal Nutrition
keyIdea: Animals, including humans, need the right types and amounts of nutrition from food they eat — they cannot make their own food the way green plants can.
familyTip: At a meal, name the groups on the plate (fruit/veg, protein, grains, dairy). Ask: could an animal make that food from sunlight alone?

lab.caption: Flagship lab: balanced plate, sort protein, plant maker vs animal eater, right amounts, catch sunlight myth.

kid: Animals, including people, need food to stay healthy.
The right types means a mix — fruit and veg, protein, grains and dairy — not only one group.
The right amounts means a sensible mix over the day, not only sweets or skipping food.
Green plants can make food with light and water. Animals cannot, so they must eat.
adult: NC Y3 Animals including humans: animals, including humans, need the right types and amount of nutrition, and they cannot make their own food — they get nutrition from what they eat. Distinct from What Living Things Need, Herbivores/Carnivores/Omnivores, and Simple Food Chains.
Words: nutrition, balanced, food group, protein. Common mistakes: thinking animals make food from sunlight; treating only sweets as enough; ignoring amounts.
In the lab your child fills a four-group plate, sorts a food, chooses animal-as-eater, picks right amounts, spots the sunlight myth, and orders the key ideas.

practice.hint: Think about what animals must do that green plants need not do the same way.
practice.explain: Animals cannot make food from sunlight; they get nutrition by eating.

practice.hint: Right types means more than one kind of food.
practice.explain: Right types means mixing groups such as fruit/veg, protein and grains.

practice.prompt: You plan {a} protein bites and {b} fruit bites. Bites in total?

practice.explain: {a} protein plus {b} fruit makes {=a+b} bites — a simple mix of types.
